subject: Post-demo: perf targets & dedicated sizing — technical recap
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Ava Morales <ava@edgescale.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: perf targets & dedicated sizing — technical recap

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and helpful context on the streaming UX and latency requirements. Quick recap of what we heard on the call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Performance / SLO targets you confirmed
   - Streaming-first-byte target: <= 120ms
   - Streaming steady-state chunk latency: <= 60ms
   - Non-streaming generation (batch responses) p95: <= 250ms for single-turn prompts
   - Expected steady concurrency: 40–60 concurrent sessions during peak; occasional spikes to ~120 for short bursts

2) Workload shape
   - Avg tokens per session: 150–300 per minute (mostly short interactive chat turns)
   - Typical sequence lengths: 128–1024 tokens (most under 512)

3) Sizing signals we discussed (prelim)
   - GPU candidates: H100 (best single-stream perf, higher cost), A100 80GB (mature, predictable), L4/L40s (cost-effective for smaller contexts)
   - KV cache / context window concerns: if you land on models > 4k context we’ll bias toward 80GB-class cards or sharded deployments

4) Proposed validation plan (what we’d run for a Dedicated evaluation)
   - 24–48 hour soak + 1-hour stress ramp to validate p95 under steady concurrency and burst profile
   - Workloads: mix of streaming sessions and short non-streaming calls; synthetic traffic mirrors recorded demo trace
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec throughput, GPU utilization, memory/KV cache behavior, error/retry rates

5) Ask from EdgeScale
   - Please confirm whether first-byte <= 120ms is mandatory or a target goal for the pilot
   - Are there any maximum-context models you intend to use (>8k) or will you be within 4k for the PoC?

Next steps
   - Diego and Marcus will propose a concrete Dedicated topology and required reserved throughput by EOD tomorrow (we’ll include an H100 vs A100 comparison plus an L4 cost option).
   - If this looks good, we’ll provision a short Dedicated evaluation window and run the soak/stress test with your team on the target week (propose Jun 29–30).
   - I’ve attached the demo metrics screenshot and a short PoC plan draft for your review.

Regards,

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- First-byte <= 120ms is an aspirational requirement for the chat product. For GA we’d like to hold that level, but for the PoC we can accept up to 150ms as a hard ceiling while we validate tail behavior.
- Context windows: our current plan is to use models up to 8k for a small subset of users, but the majority of sessions will be under 4k. If the PoC can demonstrate scalable behavior for those heavier sessions that’s ideal.
- Compliance: we will need SOC 2 evidence before moving to an enterprise contract — can you point me to the attestation and any encryption/KMS docs?

We’re supportive of the Jun 29–30 window. Please send the proposed topology and any requirements for data/sandbox accounts and we’ll confirm calendar invites.

—Ava

Hi Ava / Jasmine — quick technical notes after reviewing the call recording and the demo metrics: 

Short answers up front: yes — we can target the PoC to show first-byte <=150ms (as Ava requested) and exercise the 8k paths. For long-term GA-level p95 <=120ms at your concurrency we’ll recommend a different Dedicated topology.

GPU tradeoffs (summary):
- H100 (best perf per stream for FP16 / BF16 workloads; typically fewer cards required to meet low-latency p95 but higher hourly cost). Good when you need single-session latency SLAs under heavy KV/cache or >4k context.
- A100 80GB (very stable and predictable; strong for batched workloads and large contexts; larger fleet may be needed vs H100 for identical single-stream p95).
- L4 / L40s (cost-efficient for low-memory models and high-concurrency scenarios where you can quantize; not ideal if you plan to push many >4k-context sessions).

Sizing note (prelim — we’ll run micro-benchmarks to confirm):
- If majority is streaming + p95 target 120–150ms at 50 concurrent: start with 2x H100 nodes (pooled to serve ~50 concurrent interactive sessions) and run ramp tests. If budget-constrained, 4x A100 80GB is a reasonable alternative for equivalent throughput but expect slightly higher batching latency tuning.

Validation mechanics:
- We’ll provide a test harness you can run in your environment (or we run against the Dedicated endpoint) to reproduce traces captured in your demo.
- We’ll measure first-byte, steady-state chunks, and p95/p99 under the exact concurrency profile you provided.

Action items from us:
- Marcus: create the PoC topology doc with instance counts, estimated reserved throughput, and a cost outline (will include H100 / A100 / L4 options).
- Jasmine: coordinate kickoff and confirm test window (Jun 29–30).

Diego
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
